verdicts.note: KEY RECORD. Psychotropic drug use and FERTILITY PROBLEMS among male subjects. A fertility outcome rather than a semen parameter, and the exposure is the drug class.
Puberty onset and reproductive function in animals. Wall 7.
Contraceptive method and fecundity. A.2's.
Title is the single word 'Antidepressants', no venue, no abstract. Unroutable on the visible record.
Twin pregnancy after subfertility treatment. Wall 5.
Causes, management and prevention review.
Functional impairment and painful physical symptoms.
Follicular progesterone and IVF outcome. Wall 5.
Textbook chapter on infertility and ART.
South African paediatric and adolescent utilisation. Rare non-OECD prevalence.
Explicitly frames dysfunction as a symptom of depression first and a drug effect second. Wall 1 at link 1.
Major malformations. Wall 4.

Pregnancy-related DISCONTINUATION of antidepressants. Quantifies the exposure-measurement threat the scope document names: women stop at pregnancy recognition, and plausibly at pregnancy intention, so register exposure is endogenous to fertility intention.
First-trimester exposure. Wall 4.
GAD diagnosis and treatment.
Hypospadias. Wall 4.
Enteric nervous system after in utero exposure. Wall 4.
Fertility and Sterility pilot on SSRIs and, from the venue and title stem, semen quality. No abstract on the record; retrieve to confirm the outcome.
SSRI and IVF outcome. Wall 5; admissible only as PARAMETER_HAZARD_CLINICAL if the estimand turns out to be conception rather than treatment success.

Vilazodone versus citalopram and paroxetine on 'sexual behaviors'. Psychopharmacology publishes both human and rodent behavioural work and the visible record does not name the species. SPECIES CHECK FAILS ON THE VISIBLE RECORD, which is exactly the case Wall 7 says not to guess.
Prepubertal male rats. Wall 7.
AISD and treatment ADHERENCE. Bears on exposure duration: dysfunction shortens episodes, which shortens the exposure the deflator divides by.
Drug Safety, male patients AFTER INITIATING treatment. A new-user design at link 1.
Bioinformatic mechanism of depression on spermatogenesis.
Sexual side effects under treatment.
Oxidative stress and male infertility generally.
Alwan et al. 2007 NEJM. Wall 4, and a Tier A routing decoy recovered here inside the frame.
Impact of MENTAL ILLNESS on sexual dysfunction. The disorder's own effect at link 1, which is the baseline the drug effect is measured against.
Problems with long-term SSRI treatment; duration and persistence.
Pregnancy outcome with the ROLE OF MATERNAL DEPRESSION separated. Wall 1's design on Wall 4's outcome, which is this literature's characteristic shape: the right method applied to the wrong question.
Bupropion for SSRI side effects.
Drugs and drug abuse in male reproductive physiology; antidepressants as one entry.
Pharmacological potentiation study. Wall 7.
Adjunctive bupropion for male dysfunction.
Maternal SSRI use and miscarriage. Wall 3; cross-file to B.5, no recall credit here.
Cervical mucus and daily fecundability.

KEY DESIGN. Citalopram and fluoxetine on sexual behaviour in HEALTHY MEN. No indication, therefore no confounding by indication: the cleanest isolation of the pharmacological effect anywhere in the frame, and it sits at link 1 rather than at fertility.
Frequency of TESD in randomised trials versus in practice. The ascertainment gap measured across study designs.
Biometrics: daily conception probabilities, relaxing the independence-across-acts assumption. The link-3 non-linearity stated formally.
General infertility overview.
Counselling in infertility treatment.
SARS-CoV-2 and male infertility.

KEY HISTORICAL BASELINE. Fertility of psychiatric first admissions in Norway, 1936-1975. The indication's fertility effect measured across a window that ENDS before SSRIs existed, which makes it a clean pre-exposure counterfactual for the timing wall.
Fertility and Sterility: self-reported stress, anxiety and depression against a fertility endpoint. No abstract on the record.
Immunohistochemistry in an animal model. Wall 7.
Transgender adolescent semen quality.
Psychosocial stress and semen quality in FERTILE men. The disorder-side exposure with a mechanism outcome.
Fertility preservation in transgender women.
Psychosocial aspects of ART.
Sperm chromatin damage and fertility, no medication exposure.
SCSA in the fertility clinic.
Herbal stress control in ART.

1963 Science estimate of the DURATION OF SPERMATOGENESIS. Fixes the exposure window any semen-parameter study must respect: an exposure shorter than one spermatogenic cycle cannot show its full effect, and several of the mechanism records do not respect it.
Attachment and sexuality in infertility.

KEY BASELINE RECORD. Depression and the LIKELIHOOD OF HAVING CHILDREN, nationwide register. The indication's effect on the review's own outcome; pairs with the Norwegian and Swedish register records to bound what B.7 must net out.
Nonsurgical management of oligozoospermia.

Audio-computerised self-interview versus face-to-face for sensitive data. Mode effects on self-reported sexual behaviour are the reason link-1 and link-2 measurements are not comparable across studies.
Dysfunction in OCD and panic disorder, indications other than depression, so the untreated baseline differs.
Mobile phones and semen parameters.
Pregnancy-length measurement error, last menstrual period versus ultrasound. Bears on any exposure window defined relative to conception.
